name: Celestial Pact (Divine Contract System)
summary: A contract-bound Authority that lets the bearer exercise a patron's celestial jurisdiction through vows, service, and negotiated divine law.
description: Celestial Pact is an Authority that binds the bearer to a higher celestial being through a formal contract of service and delegated jurisdiction. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command through patron-backed clauses, divine obligations, and lawful access to a specific heavenly domain rather than through generic blessing alone. The bearer becomes a mortal instrument who can invoke their patron's sanctioned powers within the scope of the pact. Its progression bias favors obedience, negotiated favor, visible service, and the careful management of duties rather than free personal ambition. The Authority is strongest when the bearer honors contract terms, fulfills patron errands, and acts within the pact's recognized sphere. The main tradeoff is dependency, because power is mediated by relationship, behavior, and the patron's willingness to continue investing authority into the mortal vessel. In the world, Celestial Pact should feel both sacred and unsettling because it makes a person into a living embassy for a higher being. It remains lore-safe because the pact delegates bounded authority, remains contestable or revocable, and keeps the bearer beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Receive authority through a living contract that specifies the patron's domain, the bearer's obligations, and the lawful shape of granted miracles.
Fulfill pact duties, complete patron missions, and cultivate renown or worship so the contract deepens rather than stagnates.
Invoke the pact's granted jurisdiction in moments where the patron's authority is recognized and the bearer is willing to pay the relational price.
Trigger Celestial Pact (Divine Contract System)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants a binding contract, first-tier boons, and a clear set of duties that define what the pact will and will not support.
Mid progression expands into stronger delegated judgments, patron channels, and the ability to negotiate amendments or deepen clauses in the relationship.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying pact envoy whose presence can bring a slice of a higher being's order into mortal affairs.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Every visible miracle reminds everyone nearby that your patron has interests in this world and has chosen you as an instrument for them.
The more authority you wield, the more you must ask whether the pact is a partnership, a leash, or something more intimate and dangerous than either.
Other churches, pacts, and celestial intermediaries all have opinions about who should be allowed to negotiate with heaven directly.
questHooks: Renegotiate a pact clause before your patron's latest demand destroys the last part of your life that still feels human.
Outmaneuver a rival envoy whose contract covers the same domain but interprets divine duty in the opposite way.
Recover a lost covenant tablet that proves your patron once promised more mercy than their current clergy are willing to allow.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Celestial Pact can support contract clauses, duty-driven quest rewards, delegated miracles, and patron-specific authority actions. It gives divine service a negotiable structure instead of only a vague blessing. That makes the relationship itself a source of power and tension. It also supports strong variation between different patrons without changing the core category.

In narrative and quests, it enables envoy drama, contract renegotiation, faith schisms, and intimate conflict between devotion and autonomy. The bearer can use the pact to save cities or become trapped by escalating holy demands. They may also discover that their patron's true agenda is nothing like what the church teaches. That creates rich interpersonal and theological stakes.

In implementation, it maps well to pact clauses, duty completion, patron favor, revocation states, and domain-specific miracle payloads. Those hooks can feed quest systems, narrative prompts, faction politics, and ritual gating without requiring a bespoke pipeline for every deity. They also create meaningful failure states when the pact sours. That makes the Authority robust and reusable.

Its limitation-aware use comes from making power relational and conditional. The player should feel mighty when the pact is honored and deeply constrained when its obligations cut against convenience or conscience. That preserves the authority fantasy while keeping the higher being genuinely higher. The best version feels like wielding borrowed jurisdiction under a living contract.
limits: The pact only authorizes actions within the patron's delegated domain and can refuse support outside its lawful clauses.
Broken duties, theological conflict, or a damaged relationship with the patron can sharply reduce access to power.
Rival contracts, anti-divine zones, and institutions that reject the pact's legitimacy can meaningfully contest its effects.
costs: The bearer owes service, obedience, and often public representation to a patron whose priorities may not align with mortal comfort.
Using pact authority openly creates factional conflict because each miracle advances not only the bearer but the patron's agenda.
Renegotiation, revocation, or breach can carry spiritual penalties far harsher than ordinary resource depletion.
worldCompatibility: Celestial Pact governs delegated divine jurisdiction through contract and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the highest cosmic order.
It is compatible with patron quests, miracle systems, theology conflict, and religious politics because it commands a bounded celestial office.
Its power remains coherent because it depends on clauses, duties, favor, and contestable legitimacy rather than unrestricted holy access.
factionReactions: Rulers and institutions will treat Celestial Pact (Divine Contract System) as a political event, not just a combat trait.
Rival elites will test whether Celestial Pact (Divine Contract System) deserves recognition or suppression.

name: Dark Covenant (Accursed Blessing)
summary: A bargain-bound Authority that grants forbidden blessings through an active relationship with dark, predatory, or accursed powers.
description: Dark Covenant is an Authority founded on sanctioned exchange with ominous, forbidden, or predatory powers. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants a recognized right to invoke and enforce dark terms within a bounded relationship rather than building an entire independent progression engine. The bearer receives blessings, force multipliers, or law-bending clauses, but only through a living contract with appetite, debt, and metaphysical enforcement. Its progression bias favors decisive bargains, short-term leverage, and morally dangerous efficiency rather than clean sustainable advancement. The main tradeoff is obligation, because every gift implies counter-demand, and the covenant grows more intimate and expensive as the bearer leans on it. In the world, Dark Covenant is feared because it creates results too useful to ignore and costs too terrible to normalize. It is also politically ambiguous, since some cultures see it as blasphemy while others treat it as an old and respectable technology of survival. It remains lore-safe because the covenant always binds both parties inside terms, and because even powerful accursed patrons operate below the Void ceiling and can be resisted, out-negotiated, or starved.
coreLoop: Invoke contract clauses that trade permission, sacrifice, debt, or taboo offerings for immediate accursed power.
Manage the covenant relationship so the patron's hunger, personality, and demands remain exploitable rather than overwhelming.
Choose which bargains to accept, delay, reinterpret, or resist as the Authority grows stronger and more invasive.
Trigger Dark Covenant (Accursed Blessing)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early progression grants controlled blessings, curse clauses, and limited patron interventions that feel powerful but survivable.
Mid progression deepens the relationship into a true covenant with named terms, escalating debt, and patron-specific manifestations of authority.
Late progression creates terrifying leverage where one bargain can swing a war, save a city, or doom a soul depending on what the bearer agrees to pay.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The Authority always forces the question of whether survival purchased through darkness is wisdom, weakness, or the beginning of surrender.
Patrons are never neutral sources of power, which means every miracle risks becoming a negotiation scene disguised as combat utility.
Observers may fear the bearer less for what they can do now than for what they might be asked to become later.
questHooks: Renegotiate a covenant clause before the promised price comes due in a way that would destroy someone you were trying to protect.
Track down a prior covenant bearer whose failed bargains left loopholes, warnings, and enemies still hunting the contract line.
Choose whether to accept an emergency patron gift that can save the region now but will bind you to a darker long-term obligation.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Dark Covenant is excellent for high-tension choice design because power comes with attached terms instead of clean cooldowns. The bearer can take a dangerous bargain for immediate survival, mobility, damage, curse immunity, or monstrous transformation while knowing the patron will demand something later. This makes every surge feel dramatic instead of routine. It also supports distinct covenant styles based on the patron involved.

In narrative and quest design, the Authority is rich because it naturally creates debt arcs, loophole hunts, patron interventions, and moral arguments over acceptable price. The protagonist may save a town and still lose trust because of what they had to promise in return. That keeps dark power socially real. It also prevents the blessing from becoming just another buff source.

In implementation, Dark Covenant maps well to pact-state tracking, owed costs, triggered clauses, corruption pressure, and relationship logic with sentient powers. This gives designers a clean structure for patron identity and repayment cadence. It also distinguishes the Authority from generic cursed transformation kits. The mechanics stay anchored in contract law and consequence.

In long-form progression, the Authority remains compelling because it can evolve into partnership, addiction, rivalry, manipulation, or attempted emancipation from the patron. Every stronger clause increases leverage and danger at the same time. That preserves tension even when the power is impressive. It also gives the narrator an enduring antagonist or uneasy ally built directly into the kit.
limits: The Authority only functions through a living contract, so if the patron is starved, blocked, out-negotiated, or severed, access can collapse abruptly.
Every blessing arrives with scope and terms, meaning the bearer cannot simply take dark power without also accepting conditions and exposure.
Patrons are clever, hungry, or ideological, so careless bargains may win the moment while sabotaging the future.
costs: Every meaningful use creates debt, corruption pressure, sacrifice demand, or social stain that must eventually be faced instead of ignored.
The stronger the blessing, the less likely its price is to remain abstract; bodies, loyalties, oaths, and entire communities can become collateral.
Public knowledge of the covenant invites fear, holy retaliation, opportunistic manipulation, and scrutiny from anyone who knows dark patrons never give freely.
worldCompatibility: Dark Covenant governs bounded exchange with accursed powers while remaining beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and all higher law.
It is compatible with curse, sacrifice, relationship, corruption, and desperation systems because each already depends on negotiated price and consequence.
The Authority is potent but constrained, since every blessing is mediated by terms rather than granted as unanswerable cosmic supremacy.
factionReactions: Holy orders, purification sects, and fearful communities often treat the bearer as a contamination risk even when the covenant saves lives.
Pragmatic rulers, warlords, and desperate survivors may tolerate or even sponsor the Authority when results matter more than purity.
Cults and rival patrons become intensely interested because anyone carrying a dark covenant is proof that bargains with the abyss can be made to work.

name: Star-Scion Matrix (Constellation Bond)
summary: A starline Authority that seats the bearer beneath a specific celestial body or constellation and lets its law descend through them.
description: Star-Scion Matrix is an Authority that links the bearer's soul to a specific star, constellation, or celestial principle with ruling significance. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command through starline inheritance, astral precedence, and direct descent of a bounded celestial law. The bearer becomes a scion, not merely a mage, meaning their bond carries recognized weight with omens, navigators, cults, and other sky-touched powers. Its progression bias favors celestial timing, identity alignment, and the disciplined cultivation of a star-specific office rather than broad generic spell growth. The Authority is strongest when the bearer's actions resonate with the bonded star's symbolic nature and the current sky supports that resonance. The main tradeoff is cyclic vulnerability, because eclipses, adverse alignments, daylight conditions, or starline corruption can sharply alter performance. In the world, Star-Scion Matrix should feel aristocratic and cosmic at once because it makes the bearer a living extension of a star's will or meaning. It remains lore-safe because the Authority governs a bounded celestial lineage and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the highest law of the heavens.
coreLoop: Cultivate resonance with the bonded star or constellation until its law can descend through the scion in stable, named expressions.
Use celestial events, night conditions, and symbolic acts aligned with the starline to deepen command and unlock stronger manifestations.
Protect the star bond from eclipse, corruption, rival scions, and misalignment that would turn inherited law against the bearer.
Trigger Star-Scion Matrix (Constellation Bond)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants an identifiable starline bond, a first descended aspect, and practical influence over travel, combat, or fate in the star's lane.
Mid progression expands into stronger aspect descent, star-path travel, and more explicit authority over those who recognize the same celestial order.
Late progression turns the bearer into a radiant scion whose presence can make whole factions read the sky differently around them.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: Every celestial event becomes personal once your life is visibly chained to the mood and motion of one starline.
Rival scions, astrologers, and omencasters may see you as heir, usurper, or catastrophic omen depending on what your star means to them.
The more deeply the Matrix descends, the harder it becomes to tell where your ambitions end and your star's pattern begins.
questHooks: Reignite a dimming starline before your authority collapses and your enemies claim the sky has abandoned you.
Contest a rival scion during a rare conjunction that will decide whose interpretation of the same constellation becomes dominant.
Retrieve a fallen fragment of your bonded star from a crater cult that believes no mortal should carry that much sky inside them.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Star-Scion Matrix can support starline resonance, celestial event spikes, descended aspects, and role-specific sky authority. It gives cosmic builds a lineage-and-office identity instead of only broad astral spectacle. That makes timing and symbolism matter mechanically. It also creates strong seasonal and environmental flavor.

In narrative and quests, it enables omen wars, fallen-star expeditions, lineage drama, and characters whose destinies are publicly legible in the night sky. The bearer can become a cherished sign of hope or a feared harbinger depending on what their star historically means. They may also discover that their starline has obligations older than any nation. That gives the Authority rich mythic texture.

In implementation, it maps well to celestial alignment tags, event modifiers, aspect unlocks, and rivalry hooks between scions. Those hooks can feed encounter bonuses, travel systems, quest generation, and narrator framing without requiring a full astronomy sandbox. They also pair neatly with prophecy and constellation content. That makes the Authority flexible but still concrete.

Its limitation-aware use comes from making sky favor cyclical and interpretive. The player should feel amplified under the right heavens and markedly strained when misaligned or eclipsed. That preserves the prestige of star descent without turning the bond into uninterrupted cosmic dominance. The strongest version feels like carrying a star's office through changing skies.
limits: Starline power depends on resonance, timing, and the specific celestial body or constellation that legitimizes the bearer.
Eclipses, corrupted skies, hostile alignments, and broken symbolic conduct can all disrupt descent quality.
The Matrix does not grant equal command over every celestial principle; it remains bound to the bonded star's nature and inherited lane.
costs: Maintaining resonance demands ritual care, symbolic discipline, and adaptation to celestial cycles the bearer cannot control.
Publicly visible sky-omens make secrecy difficult and attract rivals, cults, and institutions invested in controlling celestial legitimacy.
A damaged starline bond can destabilize identity, fate, and magic all at once because so much of the self is now tied to a higher pattern.
worldCompatibility: Star-Scion Matrix governs bounded celestial lineage and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the deepest order of the heavens.
It is compatible with omens, celestial events, prophecy systems, and night-biased combat because it commands a specific astral office.
Its power stays coherent because it depends on resonance, alignment, and star-specific legitimacy rather than universal cosmic control.
factionReactions: Rulers and institutions will treat Star-Scion Matrix (Constellation Bond) as a political event, not just a combat trait.
Rival elites will test whether Star-Scion Matrix (Constellation Bond) deserves recognition or suppression.

name: Summoned Hero (System-Mandated Savior)
summary: A world-sanctioned Authority that appoints the bearer as a recognized hero and grants narrow but terrifying savior-grade legitimacy.
description: Summoned Hero is an Authority that installs the bearer into a world-recognized role of sanctioned salvation. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command through title, mandate, and role legitimacy rather than through a free-floating System of personal growth alone. The bearer is not simply powerful; they become the authorized hero for a specific crisis, enemy class, or era-defining threat. Its progression bias favors heroic milestones, public victories, and fulfilling the role's sanctioned duties rather than unrestricted self-direction. The Authority becomes most potent against the threat profile it was summoned or anointed to answer, which keeps its savior-grade power from dissolving into generic supremacy. The main tradeoff is burden of role, because everyone from kings to commoners begins projecting expectation, gratitude, fear, and control onto the person carrying the title. In the world, Summoned Hero should feel both inspirational and destabilizing because once a world has named its savior, many institutions stop behaving as if ordinary politics still apply. It remains lore-safe because the hero's title governs a bounded role with specific enemies, rites, and duties, and because even a sanctioned savior remains beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Answer hero-mandated threats, complete role-defining quests, and prove to the world that the title's legitimacy is not misplaced.
Convert major victories into stronger hero rights such as relic access, ally-rally effects, and sharper advantages against the sanctioned enemy profile.
Balance personal will against the crushing expectations of rulers, systems, and civilians who all think the hero exists for their salvation first.
Trigger Summoned Hero (System-Mandated Savior)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants the hero title, access to role-locked relics or skills, and strong leverage against the first crisis the summoning was meant to solve.
Mid progression expands into broader hero rights, visible aura effects, and milestone unlocks tied to defeating designated calamities or lords.
Late progression turns the bearer into a living symbol whose title can rally armies, terrify villain factions, and reshape whole wars around their presence.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: The title turns every victory into public myth and every failure into a political emergency that no one will let stay private.
People saved by the hero may worship, resent, or try to own the person behind the role once their survival starts depending on it.
The deeper you grow into the title, the more dangerous it becomes to ask whether the world wanted a savior or only a weapon.
questHooks: Choose whether to keep obeying the summons after learning the world lied about who the true enemy was.
Recover a role-locked relic before a rival claimant proves the hero title can be transferred or stolen.
Defeat the designated calamity only to discover that fulfilling the role may erase the part of you that ever wanted to go home.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Summoned Hero can support role-locked quests, anti-calamity bonuses, relic permissions, hero aura skills, and milestone-based authority growth. It gives isekai savior fantasy a lawful structure instead of only fast leveling and generic chosen-one perks. That makes the role readable to both systems and NPCs. It also supports strong factional reactions by title alone.

In narrative and quests, it enables summon politics, false-hero disputes, kingdom manipulation, and the pain of realizing salvation can be a coercive job. The bearer can become beloved, exploited, or both at once. They may also decide the title itself is a prison even while others still need what it grants. That gives the Authority excellent dramatic range.

In implementation, it maps well to title flags, calamity-specific bonuses, role milestones, relic access, and world-recognition events. Those hooks can feed quest systems, combat modifiers, UI labels, and narrator framing without demanding a separate hero-only engine. They also create great synergy with kingdoms, war arcs, and villain factions. That makes the Authority highly practical to integrate.

Its limitation-aware use comes from keeping the hero title tied to designated threats and public role legitimacy. The player should feel empowered when confronting the crisis they were named for and much less absolute outside that lane. That preserves the savior fantasy while preventing it from flattening the rest of the setting. The strongest version feels like sanctioned heroism under pressure, not generic protagonist invincibility.
limits: Hero-grade authority is strongest against the sanctioned threat class, role-defined crises, and situations where the title is publicly or ritually recognized.
Outside the role's lane, the bearer retains strength and prestige but loses much of the title's special command weight.
False summoning, rival claimants, title corruption, or public delegitimization can all weaken the authority dramatically.
costs: Carrying the hero title invites impossible expectations from rulers, allies, and populations who now view the bearer as a public solution.
Every visible use of hero authority intensifies political attempts to direct, own, or sacrifice the person behind the role.
If the role proves fraudulent, misguided, or morally compromised, the backlash can be social, spiritual, and existential all at once.
worldCompatibility: Summoned Hero governs a bounded savior office and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the highest order that defines destiny and world law.
It is compatible with summoning plots, calamity arcs, relic gating, and public-legitimacy systems because it commands a specific role rather than free universal privilege.
Its power stays coherent because it depends on title, threat profile, milestones, and recognition instead of unrestricted protagonist supremacy.
factionReactions: Rulers and institutions will treat Summoned Hero (System-Mandated Savior) as a political event, not just a combat trait.
Rival elites will test whether Summoned Hero (System-Mandated Savior) deserves recognition or suppression.

name: Territory Lord Interface (Base-Building Sovereign)
summary: A governance Authority that lets the bearer issue lordly commands through a territory-management interface tied to lawful domain growth.
description: Territory Lord Interface is an Authority that converts rulership and land stewardship into a direct command layer the bearer can access. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants jurisdiction over buildings, projects, labor assignment, and local edicts inside a recognized territory. The bearer does not merely manage a city more efficiently, but gains the lawful right to impose structured development priorities that reshape local productivity and defense. Its progression bias favors planning, logistics, and institutional growth rather than free-roaming heroics. The Authority is strongest where the bearer truly holds recognized land, resources, and subjects willing or forced to live under its interface. The main tradeoff is dependence on governance, because neglected territory, bad policy, corruption, or resource starvation can turn the interface from miracle into administrative disaster. In the world, Territory Lord Interface should feel revolutionary because it gives one ruler simulation-grade leverage over real settlements and warfronts. It remains lore-safe because the interface only commands a bounded territory and its lawful projects, and because even its best governance remains beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Claim or maintain a lawful territory, then use the interface to assign projects, structures, labor priorities, and regional bonuses.
Convert territory output into stronger lordly authority, better infrastructure, and more ambitious projects that reshape local life.
Balance prosperity, defense, and legitimacy so the same tools that can build a kingdom do not instead automate collapse.
Trigger Territory Lord Interface (Base-Building Sovereign)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth unlocks basic build orders, resource-routing panels, and local buffs that make a small settlement meaningfully easier to protect and grow.
Mid progression expands into specialized districts, militia logistics, outpost links, and stronger law-of-the-land effects across the domain.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying territorial executive who can scale a frontier holding into a fortified polity at unnatural speed.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: To your people the interface looks like miraculous governance, while rivals see it as a cheating machine for statecraft.
Every improvement to the land changes what kind of ruler you are becoming, because optimization always has a human cost somewhere.
The better the territory runs, the less room there is to pretend your political decisions are merely personal preferences.
questHooks: Stabilize a starving domain before the same interface that made it prosper also makes its collapse impossibly efficient.
Break a rival lord's project chain before their engineered border towns become an unassailable machine state.
Choose whether to spend your next major build phase on walls, hospitals, shrines, or extraction knowing one neglected need will erupt later.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Territory Lord Interface can support build queues, project unlocks, law-of-the-land buffs, and territory-linked army or economy bonuses. It gives rulership a real command identity instead of only menu management. That makes settlements and borders strategically meaningful. It also ties local development back to the character's authority in a satisfying way.

In narrative and quests, it enables frontier governance, city-building politics, rationing crises, and the temptation to optimize people like resources. The bearer can save a region through disciplined planning or become feared for what their efficient rule demands. That gives the Authority strong social texture. It also naturally supports long arcs of expansion and backlash.

In implementation, it maps well to domain projects, regional modifiers, structure tiers, labor allocation, and outpost networks. Those hooks can enrich economy, quests, faction reputation, and narrator summaries without requiring a brand-new grand strategy game inside the repo. They also integrate cleanly with existing territory and dungeon-adjacent systems. That makes the Authority highly shippable.

Its limitation-aware use comes from keeping the interface dependent on real land and real governance. The player should feel brilliant at home and exposed once removed from the machine they built. That preserves the fantasy of lawful lordship rather than letting it become portable omnipotence. The strongest version feels like command rooted in institutions, not magic menus detached from consequence.
limits: The interface only reaches full authority inside recognized territory with functioning infrastructure, resources, and local control.
Projects can fail, stall, or backfire if labor, morale, logistics, or legitimacy are mismanaged.
Rapid expansion creates administrative drag that can outpace the bearer's ability to govern what they have built.
costs: Every territory gain multiplies responsibility, defense burden, and the number of people harmed if policy goes wrong.
Building fast consumes resources and may create dependency on systems that collapse if the lord is absent or defeated.
Political enemies, corruption, and sabotage become constant pressure once the interface starts producing visible advantage.
worldCompatibility: Territory Lord Interface governs bounded settlement administration and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the highest order of reality and sovereignty.
It is compatible with domain management, economy, militia logistics, and frontier politics because it commands a specific civic territory.
Its power stays coherent because it depends on land, resources, legitimacy, and administrative capacity rather than free instant kingdom creation anywhere.
factionReactions: Rulers and institutions will treat Territory Lord Interface (Base-Building Sovereign) as a political event, not just a combat trait.
Rival elites will test whether Territory Lord Interface (Base-Building Sovereign) deserves recognition or suppression.

name: Domain Sovereign (Personal Domain Expansion)
summary: A bounded-field Authority that lets the bearer impose a personal domain whose laws locally outrank ordinary combat assumptions.
description: Domain Sovereign is an Authority that allows the bearer to project a bounded personal domain governed by their own declared law. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command over a specific field of space where the bearer's rule has precedence, rather than granting unrestricted control over reality at large. Inside that domain, conditions can be modified to reflect the sovereign's principle, such as priority of motion, heat tolerance, sensory distortion, or suppression of enemy technique lanes. Its progression bias favors territorial timing, decisive activation, and the sharpening of one governing law rather than broad utility across every situation. The Authority is strongest when the bearer can force enemies to remain inside the field long enough for its rule to matter. The main tradeoff is boundedness, because the domain costs heavily to establish, can be contested by stronger fields, and loses much of its terror once opponents escape or refuse the terms. In the world, Domain Sovereign should feel awe-inspiring because it visibly announces that someone has become a local ruler of conditions. It remains lore-safe because the domain is spatially bounded, law-limited, and still subordinate to Void, Grandmother Void, and stronger sovereign orders.
coreLoop: Declare or unfold a bounded domain whose governing law favors the bearer and pressures enemies to fight on its terms.
Exploit the domain's altered rules before opponents can break, escape, or overwrite the field with stronger authority.
Refine the governing law over time so the domain becomes sharper, more recognizable, and more difficult to contest.
Trigger Domain Sovereign (Personal Domain Expansion)'s authority protocol by completing a focused objective tied to your current build.
progression: Early growth grants a small but reliable domain with one clean law that changes how a duel or skirmish must be fought.
Mid progression expands field stability, layered law effects, and the ability to carry the domain into more hostile or crowded battle spaces.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying battlefield sovereign whose activation can redefine the meaning of terrain itself for everyone nearby.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: When your domain opens, witnesses feel the world become someone else's courtroom, temple, or killing ground for a few terrible moments.
Rivals who survive it will obsess over learning exactly what law you imposed and how to deny it next time.
The more absolute your field feels, the more dangerous it becomes to believe your rule should continue once the boundary ends.
questHooks: Win a clash between rival domains where the outcome will determine whose local law becomes dominant in a sacred battleground.
Stabilize a domain principle that keeps mutating under pressure before it tears your own battlefield advantage apart.
Choose whether to teach disciples your domain law, knowing each student risks diluting or corrupting the sovereign idea behind it.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Domain Sovereign can support activation windows, zone control, law modifiers, and duel-centric battlefield shifts. It gives personal territory play a clean authority identity separate from settlement systems. That makes timing and positioning matter sharply. It also creates strong boss-fight spectacle without losing mechanical readability.

In narrative and quests, it enables showdown scenes, doctrine clashes, sacred-site contests, and stories where one person's field changes the emotional weight of a whole encounter. The bearer can become famous for a domain that announces exactly what kind of ruler they are in miniature. They may also become feared for relying on private law too much. That gives the Authority strong visual and philosophical punch.

In implementation, it maps well to zone effects, activation states, law payloads, contest checks, and domain counters. Those hooks can enrich combat, narration, and progression with bounded logic rather than vague reality bending. They also scale nicely from duels to larger encounters. That makes the Authority practical to integrate while still feeling high tier.

Its limitation-aware use comes from keeping the field bounded and contestable. The player should feel dominant once the domain is established and immediately pressured when enemies refuse or break the terms. That preserves the sovereignty fantasy without letting it turn into perpetual control of every scene. The strongest version feels like temporary local rulership won through force and clarity.
limits: The domain only governs within its active boundary and loses leverage rapidly when enemies escape, suppress, or outlast it.
Each sovereign law must be narrow enough to remain coherent, which prevents the bearer from stacking every advantage at once.
Stronger domains, anti-field tools, and poor activation timing can all blunt or shatter the authority's effect.
costs: Opening a domain consumes significant energy, focus, and often leaves the bearer exposed if the field fails to take hold.
Maintaining layered law inside the domain strains body and will, especially against many targets or contested spaces.
The more often the bearer solves problems through private law, the more isolated and inflexible they can become outside the field.
worldCompatibility: Domain Sovereign governs bounded local lawfields and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and stronger sovereign structures.
It is compatible with duel systems, battlefield control, and authority clashes because it commands a spatially limited personal domain.
Its power stays coherent because it depends on boundary, law focus, activation cost, and contest rather than unrestricted rule over reality.
factionReactions: Rulers and institutions will treat Domain Sovereign (Personal Domain Expansion) as a political event, not just a combat trait.
Rival elites will test whether Domain Sovereign (Personal Domain Expansion) deserves recognition or suppression.

name: Nature's Avatar (World Elemental Integration)
summary: An elemental-biospheric Authority that makes the bearer a recognized voice of land, weather, and living ecological force.
description: Nature's Avatar is an Authority that binds the bearer to a major biospheric or elemental order of the world. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command over a natural domain such as forest, storm, river, growth, or beast ecology rather than broad generic spell access. The bearer becomes a recognized mouthpiece of that domain, able to summon, calm, reshape, or intensify its living processes. Its progression bias favors harmony, place-attunement, and reciprocal stewardship rather than extractive power for its own sake. The Authority is strongest where the chosen domain is vibrant, present, and not violently severed from itself by corruption or artificial suppression. The main tradeoff is reciprocity, because abusing the domain for selfish force can weaken the bond or make the natural order itself turn hostile. name: Law Manipulator (World Rule Bender)
summary: A high-order Authority that lets the bearer impose specific world-rule distortions within tightly bounded lawful scope.
description: Law Manipulator is an Authority that grants the bearer command over a small set of fundamental world rules within limited scope. It belongs in the Authority category because it governs specific laws such as weight, heat, motion, or sequence through narrow sovereign intervention rather than open-ended reality authorship. The bearer is not omniscient about law, but gains the right to impose or distort chosen rules inside a battlefield, ritual, or prepared zone. Its progression bias favors enlightenment, clarity of principle, and disciplined restriction rather than stacking every possible cheat at once. The Authority becomes strongest when the bearer understands exactly which law must bend and where the bend will matter most. The main tradeoff is precision burden, because the wrong law, the wrong scope, or the wrong timing can waste power or catastrophically destabilize the scene. In the world, Law Manipulator should feel terrifyingly intellectual because it makes a person's understanding into a direct command over what others assumed was fixed. It remains lore-safe because the Authority operates through bounded law selection, contest, and cost, and remains beneath Void and Grandmother Void.
coreLoop: Select the governing law that matters most to the current conflict or ritual instead of trying to dominate every variable at once.
Impose a bounded distortion in a defined scope where the chosen law now favors the bearer or punishes the unprepared.
Manage backlash, counter-law pressure, and the risk that the altered rule will harm allies or terrain if held too long.

progression: Early growth grants one or two modest law distortions with strict scope, duration, and cost boundaries.
Mid progression expands into sharper distortions, better law pairing, and stronger resistance against enemies who rely on one fixed rule too heavily.
Late progression turns the bearer into a feared law duelist who wins not by overpowering reality, but by choosing exactly which rule everyone must suddenly survive.
Tier I grants a baseline passive that accelerates one progression channel while introducing a clear tradeoff.
narrativeHooks: People stop calling you powerful and start calling you dangerous once they realize you can make certainty itself feel conditional.

questHooks: Steal a forbidden law-principle from an archive that executed the last person who tried to bind it.
Survive a duel against another law-bearer where victory goes to whoever defines the battlefield's governing rule first.
Decide whether to seal a dangerous law forever or keep it because too many future crises may demand its use.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Law Manipulator can support scoped rule changes, field distortions, law-based counters, and puzzle or ritual solutions built around one decisive principle. It gives late-game intellect builds a sharp authority identity. That makes battles feel like contests of understanding rather than only stat comparison. It also works well for boss mechanics and forbidden-tech progressions.

In narrative and quests, it enables forbidden-research arcs, battlefield jurisprudence, magical accidents, and the fear that some people should simply not be allowed to edit what everyone else calls reality. The bearer can save lives by choosing the right law or ruin them by forcing the wrong one. That creates excellent tension between brilliance and hubris. It also complements the repo's cosmic hierarchy cleanly.

In implementation, it maps well to selectable law effects, scope metadata, counters, and distortion timers. Those hooks can feed combat, hazards, rituals, and narrator framing without requiring the game to support unrestricted simulation edits. They also let designers control which laws are even available. That keeps the Authority powerful and bounded.

Its limitation-aware use comes from making selection and scope matter more than raw scale. The player should feel rewarded for choosing the correct rule and punished for treating law command like a universal answer. That preserves the authority fantasy without collapsing it into free reality hacking. The strongest version feels surgical, dangerous, and earned.
limits: Only a limited number of laws can be actively manipulated, and each has strict scope, duration, and stability constraints.
Poor law selection or environmental mismatch can make a manipulation nearly useless or actively harmful.
Stronger sovereign fields, anti-law measures, and unstable terrain can resist or distort the imposed rule in return.
costs: Every manipulation burns focus and energy while inviting backlash if the world pushes the bent rule back into place.

worldCompatibility: Law Manipulator governs a bounded set of contestable world rules and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the highest cosmic order.

name: Blood Pact Warlock (Contracted Power)
summary: A dark-contract Authority that grants the bearer borrowed command through blood-sealed obligations, patron claims, and dangerous power rights.
description: Blood Pact Warlock is an Authority that binds the bearer to a patron through blood-sealed obligation and dangerous contractual power. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command through the legal and symbolic force of a blood pact, not merely by borrowing spells from something stronger. The bearer becomes an authorized vessel for a patron's dark jurisdiction, able to command pact-granted effects, entities, and sanctions within the contract's scope. Its progression bias favors negotiation, sacrifice, and increasingly severe exchanges of self or service rather than clean personal growth. The Authority is strongest when the pact is active, the debt is current, and the patron's sphere overlaps with the crisis at hand. name: Divinity Pathway

It belongs in the Path category because it is a structured route of apotheosis, not a ready-made divine Authority granted in full at the start. The bearer chooses or discovers a domain and then builds themselves into its proper vessel through deeds, followers, rites, and trials of worthiness. It also produces visible consequence, since each stage affects mobility, appetite, vulnerabilities, social access, and how different factions classify the bearer.
